items.title: Josephine Davies interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 14, 2025
items.q: You did the opposite of what Phil Woods had said about young musicians.

ctx.x: things which is of course impossible when you have both of those faculties. But it was a real struggle because I thought reading for me is as important as music in some ways, to really lose myself in a world that somebody else has imagined and then is giving to me through the means of the page, where I’m – as I’m reading their world I’m creating my own world. And I think there is something so fundamentally important about that for me that I’m not sure I could be a composer or a musician if I couldn’t experience…
You did the opposite of what Phil Woods had said about young musicians. And his advice was well if you can be a doctor or a tenor player, be the doctor. And you went the other way.

Yeah. But I’m really – it’s got to be, obviously we live in a world where there are many limitations and constraints and we have to make it work in some way and it very much is about the possibilities that you have in life and also your dependents, who is relying on you, all of that stuff. But I think the question that – I was very fortunate enough to grow up with a mother whose – without explicitly stating it – letting me know that being – finding something passionate, finding something in your life that you’re…
